raw_segments.text: Medea, he loveth to bear bravely ills like these.
But Aegius, by thy beard, O by thy knees, I pray thee, and I give me for thine own thy
O, pity one so miserable, thou never wilt stand there and see me cast out friendless
Give me a home in Athens.
By the fire of thine own hearth, O, so may thy desire of children be fulfilled of God,
Thou canst know not, even now thy prize is won.
I will make of thee a childless man no more.
The seed shall be, I swear it sown, such magic herbs I know.
